How can I prevent plant diseases?
What should I do if my leaves turn yellow?
How often should I water my crop?
How do I improve plant growth?
Type a question about your plant or crop to get advice.
💡 Advice is for general plant-care guidance. For serious crop problems, consult a local agricultural expert.

To prevent plant diseases, keep good spacing between plants, avoid watering the leaves unnecessarily, remove infected plant material, keep the growing area clean, and provide adequate sunlight and air circulation.

Yellow leaves can have several causes, including overwatering, underwatering, poor drainage, nutrient deficiency, or natural aging. Check the soil moisture first and make sure the plant has good drainage.

Watering frequency depends on the crop, soil, temperature, and weather. Check the soil before watering. Water when the upper layer of soil begins to dry, and avoid keeping the roots constantly waterlogged.

To improve plant growth, provide sufficient sunlight, suitable soil, balanced nutrients, adequate water, and good air circulation. Remove damaged leaves and monitor the plant regularly for pests or disease.

Inspect the leaves, stems, and fruit for unusual spots, discoloration, wilting, or fungal growth. Remove badly affected plant material and improve air circulation. A clear photo can also help identify the problem.

Inspect the underside of leaves and young shoots for insects or damage. Remove visible pests when possible and keep the plant healthy. Monitor the plant regularly so an infestation can be detected early.
